risks.description: The Group Application may be unsubmitted close to the immutable deadline
risks.trigger: No receipt or explicit status confirmation by 2026-08-12
risks.mitigation: Verify course-system status immediately while preparing the form and advisor path in parallel
risks.fallback: Escalate to advisor and course staff before the deadline with complete form evidence

risks.description: No authorized dataset provides every desired modality linked at patient level — confirmed 2026-08-30, not merely forecast
risks.trigger: CONFIRMED on 2026-08-30: patient-level cross-modality linkage exists only within the MIMIC family (subject_id shared by MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-CXR). CheXpert, BraTS, CT-RATE, VQA-RAD and SLAKE are separate populations and cannot be joined to it
risks.mitigation: Adopt the confirmed architecture: a patient-linked MIMIC core carrying clinical text, structured data, longitudinal history and 2D imaging, plus explicitly unlinked capability subsets for 3D and VQA. Label every result as linked-cohort or unlinked-capability evidence; never merge them into one headline score | 2026-09-21: the MIMIC core this mitigation depends on is gated by a CITI course the team has not taken. The evidence on file is Responsible Conduct of Research; PhysioNet requires 'Data or Specimens Only Research' with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology Affiliates affiliation (https://physionet.org/about/citi-course/, read 2026-09-21). Tracked as TASK-0038
risks.fallback: Narrow the evaluated modality combinations and state the limitation plainly in the Proposal and the model card, rather than implying a single-patient five-modality journey the data cannot support

risks.description: Patient identity or temporal leakage could invalidate model and product evidence
risks.trigger: A patient overlaps splits, a future-derived input is found, or a transform uses test information
risks.mitigation: Split before derivation, maintain availability/provenance ledgers, and run automated adversarial audits
risks.fallback: Invalidate affected evidence, rebuild a new data version, and rerun all dependent experiments

risks.description: Available compute may not support stable approximately 27B training and evaluation
risks.trigger: No approved hardware, budget, recovery, and time plan for approximately 27B exists at the flagship gate
risks.mitigation: Re-estimate compute, storage, and cost against 27B before any Tier 3 or Tier 4 request; validate staged recipes and prove checkpoint recovery at small scale first
risks.fallback: Deliver the strongest valid smaller open-weight model and report the scale shortfall plainly; never relabel it as approximately 27B

risks.description: Dynamic routing may collapse or provide no controlled quality-efficiency-faithfulness benefit
risks.trigger: Graphs converge, all nodes activate, replay fails, or the method loses controlled comparisons without trade-off
risks.mitigation: Use small kill tests, routing diagnostics, curricula, load/budget objectives, and matched ablations Strengthened by evidence recorded 2026-09-02: LIT-0026 reports that at fixed active parameters memorisation improves while reasoning saturates, and LIT-0034 reports hash and random-fixed routing within 1.1-2.2 perplexity of learned routing across 62 controlled runs. The project's regime is fine-tuned clinical reasoning, the unfavourable case. Baseline family 4 (random/shuffled routing) is therefore the load-bearing experiment, and which branch of G4 is primary must be predeclared before Stage C produces a number.
risks.fallback: Stop scaling and propose a bounded architecture reframing through a human decision

risks.description: Research and Innovation may drift to incompatible data, API, graph, or evaluation contracts
risks.trigger: Provider-specific fields reach clients or shared fixtures fail across adapters
risks.mitigation: Version schemas, require contract fixtures, isolate adapters, and run integration audits
risks.fallback: Freeze the last compatible contract and implement an explicit migration before further integration

risks.description: The Clinical Front Door may give false reassurance or under-triage critical simulated cases
risks.trigger: Critical sensitivity, red-flag preservation, under-triage, or false reassurance gate fails
risks.mitigation: Use independent red-flag rules, conservative escalation, abstention, human confirmation, and safety-first metrics
risks.fallback: Disable unsafe pathway output and restrict the demonstration scope until independently re-reviewed

risks.description: Compressed academic writing may consume technical critical-path capacity
risks.trigger: A deliverable enters T-7 with missing sections or an incomplete evidence inventory
risks.mitigation: Write continuously from source of truth, reserve review buffers, and assign section owners
risks.fallback: Cut P3 and P4 technical scope while preserving validity, safety, and the minimum deliverable

risks.description: External API use may create privacy, cost, availability, or provider lock-in risk
risks.trigger: A real-data request, uncapped usage, provider drift, or provider-native client field appears
risks.mitigation: Use synthetic defaults, exact approvals, cost/time limits, stable gateway contracts, and version logs
risks.fallback: Disable the external adapter and use the mock or approved local baseline provider

risks.description: The open-weight release may be blocked or narrowed by dataset licence terms
risks.trigger: CONFIRMED on 2026-08-30: every candidate except VQA-RAD (CC0) restricts use to non-commercial research. CT-RATE is CC-BY-NC-SA, whose ShareAlike term plausibly reaches derivative works. Whether the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License permits releasing model weights trained on MIMIC is undetermined — the licence governs the data and is silent on weights
risks.mitigation: Settle the PhysioNet model-weights question with PhysioNet in writing before any release is planned. Decide deliberately whether CT-RATE is worth its ShareAlike cost. Maintain licence lineage per dataset in project_state/dataset_feasibility.json and re-check it at release
risks.fallback: Release under the most restrictive applicable terms and say so plainly, or withhold weights and release only cleared code and evaluation artifacts. Never describe the release as more open than its licences permit

risks.description: Single-author documents ship without independent review, so errors reach examiners uncorrected
risks.trigger: REALISED on the Project Idea: it was written and submitted by one person with no review by a member who did not write it, so Phase 1 CONTEXT D-03 was not met. The submitted document reached the advisor with three unresolved defects — a claim of 3D CT support with no CT dataset in the candidate list, claims C-01 and C-02 left without attribution after the reference list was cut from 13 to 5, and an open-weight promise the licences may not permit. An independent reader would plausibly have caught at least one
risks.mitigation: Name a reviewer who is not the author for every graded deliverable, and make review a precondition of submission rather than a courtesy. The Proposal Report is four times the length of the Project Idea and carries more technical claims, so the same failure there is proportionally more costly TASK-0026 introduces a non-author reviewer for the TASK-0004 deliverable, which is the first time this project has built one in rather than owed one.
risks.fallback: If no reviewer is available before a deadline, submit and record explicitly in WEEKLY_STATUS that the document is unreviewed, so the gap is visible rather than silent

risks.description: Submission evidence is not captured at the moment of submission and becomes unrecoverable
risks.trigger: REALISED on the Group Application: submission is recorded only as the project owner's recollection from 2026-08-11, the receipt was never archived, and it is no longer retrievable. M0 therefore cannot close on documentary evidence and the gap is permanent
risks.mitigation: Capture the artefact at the moment of submission for every remaining deadline — the file actually sent, plus its checksum, plus any confirmation page or email — following the pattern established for the Project Idea in docs/academic/SUBMISSION_RECORD.md. Evidence gathered later is evidence that may not exist later
risks.fallback: Record the absence explicitly with its date and cause, and never let a milestone read as evidenced when it rests on recollection

risks.description: The novelty claim does not survive contact with prior work. The per-case typed dynamic DAG is a named, surveyed research area as of March 2026 (LIT-0031); typed DAG execution with replay is engineering practice (LIT-0035); per-input graph generation is peer-reviewed (LIT-0033); and MedGemma 1.5 (LIT-0014) already holds the 27B scale, open weights, 3D and longitudinal ground. What survives is a composite plus an evaluation contribution, which is weaker than a mechanism claim.
risks.trigger: Realised. Confirmed 2026-09-02 by SRCH-0001 and SRCH-0003 and recorded as twelve novelty threats in docs/research/RELATED_WORK.md. Escalates further if an examiner names a system demonstrating dynamic graph topology, typed operators and case-level adaptation together with medical multimodal breadth.
risks.mitigation: State the composite claim honestly and foreground the evaluation contribution: the workflow survey confirms zero clinical applications in the dynamic-workflow literature and names structural credit assignment as an open problem. Not one system screened scored DEMONSTRATED on equal-compute evidence.
risks.fallback: Narrow the contribution to the axes that survive, via an accepted Decision Log entry. Reframing is a valid research outcome under RESEARCH_SPEC.md; overstating is not.

risks.description: The product setting and the surveyed data setting do not match. DEC-0016 fixes the evaluated setting as emergency-department first-contact triage, but the dataset feasibility survey recorded MIMIC-IV as the hosp and icu modules only. MIMIC-IV-ED has never been surveyed and is not a candidate dataset; it appears once in the repository, as an unexecuted SRCH-0005 query string. CHIEF_COMPLAINT and TRIAGE_NOTE therefore have no recorded data source, and under-triage cannot be measured on a cohort that was never triaged.
risks.trigger: DS-0008 is not surveyed, or its survey returns that MIMIC-IV-ED cannot supply time-valid triage-point snapshots linked to the DS-0001 and DS-0002 cohort
risks.mitigation: Survey MIMIC-IV-ED as DS-0008 under the same six dimensions (TASK-0031). Its licence, patient-linkage, temporal-validity and modality dimensions do not depend on CITI and proceed now; only the access dimension waits on CITI (TASK-0011) and a human-signed DUA. Open MC-BEC (arXiv:2311.04937), the multimodal emergency-care benchmark the literature survey surfaced but did not screen.
risks.fallback: State the setting in the Proposal as the intended evaluation setting, name MIMIC-IV-ED as the intended corpus, and say plainly that the survey is outstanding. Do not present emergency-department triage as data-backed before DS-0008 exists. If MIMIC-IV-ED proves unusable, either narrow the evaluated claim to the hospital encounter the surveyed data actually covers, or report triage-point results as synthetic-only and label them as such.

risks.description: The evaluation cannot distinguish a safe system from one that escalates everything, and the cause is structural rather than a shortage of cases. Tracing innovation/gateway/safety.py: SCR-002 raises COMPLAINT_NOT_EVALUATED_BY_RULE as UNKNOWN for every CLINICAL_FRONT_DOOR request carrying a chief complaint, and SR-002 turns any UNKNOWN flag into URGENT_REVIEW and ESCALATED. Every complaint-bearing case therefore escalates by construction, independently of its content. The only route to IMMEDIATE_REVIEW is a TRIGGERED flag, and the only TRIGGERED flag produced anywhere is REQUIRED_INFORMATION_INCOMPLETE, so the top urgency level is reachable only through absent information and never through clinical severity; neither the mock nor the baseline provider ever emits TRIGGERED. under_triage_rate is consequently 0.0 by construction, and no metric in METRIC_DEFINITIONS records the opposite error. Distinct from RISK-0007, which is that the system may under-triage: this is that the evaluation could not detect it either way.
risks.trigger: Realised. EVAL-0001 reports escalation 0.83 with under-triage 0.0 and critical sensitivity 1.0, which are the values this mechanism produces whatever the cases contain.
risks.mitigation: Freeze an over_triage_rate definition before any new run, since EVALUATION_CONTRACT.md requires metrics frozen before results are inspected and adding one after seeing 0.83 would be metric-shopping. Give cases a declared band by adding expected_maximum_urgency beside expected_minimum_urgency. Then rebuild the case set (TASK-0032) knowing the number will get worse, and design the content-reading screen that makes the levels reachable (TASK-0033).
risks.fallback: Report the limitation as the finding. A measured demonstration that the deterministic screen cannot discriminate, with the mechanism named and the fix designed, is a defensible Proposal result; a rebuilt case set whose escalation rate moved for unexplained reasons is not.

risks.description: The project has two Front Doors and the safety evidence is on the one users do not see. innovation/gateway/ and innovation/frontdoor/ carry the Model Gateway, the audit log, the urgency taxonomy, uncertainty and the DAG explorer, all tested, behind the Jinja screens at /ui. innovation/v2/ behind the React workspace at /workspace is a separate implementation with its own providers, its own store and its own review flow, and innovation/config.py enables it by default while QUICKSTART.md calls /ui/v2 a recovery fallback. Verified by grep on 2026-09-16: ModelGateway, SafetyPolicy, red_flag and urgency each returned zero hits across innovation/v2/, and audit returned zero hits there as well. MODEL_API_CONTRACT.md opens by requiring every provider to implement the contract through the Model Gateway, so the default UI path violated it. The deterministic screen was connected on 2026-09-16 (both paths now call one screen_evidence), which closes A1.2 and A3.2 on v2. Two gaps remain open: v2 does not route through the Model Gateway (A0) and v2 has no audit record tying model version, provider version, reviewer identity and overrides together (A3.5). Distinct from RISK-0006, which is Research/Innovation contract drift; this is drift between two implementations inside Innovation itself.
risks.trigger: Realised and partly mitigated. The gap existed from the v2 delivery of 2026-09-12 to 2026-09-16 and was invisible because ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md was never updated by the v2 commit, so no criterion pointed at /workspace and nothing could fail.
risks.mitigation: Done: one implementation of SCR-001 and SCR-002 in innovation/gateway/safety.py:screen_evidence, called by both paths, with a regression test that fails when the v2 call is removed; the RESEARCH PROTOTYPE - HUMAN REVIEW REQUIRED banner added to v2; a per-criterion v1/v2 table added to ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md so a future divergence has something to fail against. Open: decide under DEC-0003 whether v2 routes through the Model Gateway or keeps its own provider protocol, and give v2 an audit sink either way.
risks.fallback: Demonstrate on /ui and state plainly that /workspace is the intake and review surface while the gateway path carries the audited decision. That is a weaker product story but a true one; claiming A0-A4 for /workspace without the audit record would not be.
